contract.title: Master Services Agreement — Managed Equipment Support Services (AGR-2026-47)
relevant_excerpts: 2. Scope of Services. 2.1 The Vendor shall provide to the Client consulting and managed support services as reasonably requested by the Client from time to time in connection with equipment operations, maintenance coordination, technical advisory, logistics support, and such other related services as the parties may agree (collectively, the "Services"). 2.2 The Services shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards. 2.3 The Vendor shall assign suitably qualified personnel to perform the Services and shall ensure continuity of key personnel where practicable. 2.4 Specific deliverables, service levels, and acceptance criteria for individual work streams may be documented in one or more Statements of Work executed by both parties, each of which shall be governed by and incorporated into this Agreement.

4. Fees and Invoicing. 4.1 In consideration of the Services, the Client shall pay the Vendor a monthly retainer of AUD 5,505.00 (inclusive of GST where applicable), billed in arrears within five (5) business days following the end of each calendar month of service. 4.2 Work that falls outside the scope of the retainer Services as described in Clause 2 ("Out-of-Scope Work") shall be performed only upon prior written approval of the Client and shall be invoiced on a time-and-materials basis at the rates set forth in Schedule B. 4.3 Total fees payable under this Agreement, including the retainer and any approved Out-of-Scope Work, shall not exceed AUD 81,650.00 unless the parties agree in writing to an increase. 4.4 The Vendor shall issue invoices referencing Purchase Order PO-BHGF-2026-4962 and the applicable service period. Payment terms are thirty (30) days from receipt of a valid tax invoice.

5. Acceptance. 5.1 For recurring retainer Services, deliverables shall be deemed accepted unless the Client provides written notice of non-conformance within ten (10) business days following receipt of the applicable monthly service report. 5.2 For discrete deliverables identified in a Statement of Work, the Client shall have fifteen (15) business days from delivery to review and either accept or reject the deliverable in writing, specifying with reasonable particularity any deficiencies. 5.3 If the Client does not provide written acceptance or rejection within the applicable review period, the deliverable shall be deemed accepted.

8. Changes and Out-of-Scope Work. 8.1 Either party may propose changes to the scope, schedule, or fees of the Services by submitting a written change request to the other party. 8.2 No change shall be effective, and no Out-of-Scope Work shall be commenced, until both parties have executed a written change order specifying the revised scope, any additional fees, and the impact on the Agreement term. 8.3 The Vendor shall not be entitled to compensation for any Out-of-Scope Work performed without prior written approval from an authorised representative of the Client. 8.4 Approved change orders shall be sequentially numbered and shall form part of this Agreement.

delivery_evidence.text: Vanguarda managed support cycle (28 Jun–27 Jul) completed—PM schedule updated for all active grantee sites; remote diagnostics handled for two telemetry dropouts; calibration register refreshed with July expiries flagged. No issues noted. Need to upload vendor monthly service note and route for finance approval (my delegation may be insufficient). Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AGR-2026-47.

Monthly Service Note — Managed Equipment Support Services, Climate Resilience Program
Service period: 2026-06-28 to 2026-07-27
Client: Banksia Harbour Grants Foundation Ltd
Agreement ref: AGR-2026-47

D1 – Preventive Maintenance Schedule & Coordination
- Rolling PM calendar issued 2026-06-30 covering all 14 active grantee sites.
- Confirmed upcoming service windows with site contacts at Gladstone, Mackay, Bundaberg, Hervey Bay, Townsville (North), Townsville (South), Cairns, Rockhampton, Emerald, Longreach, Ipswich, Logan, Redlands, and Gold Coast.
- Dispatch/return tracking updated in shared portal for scheduled sensor swap-outs at Mackay (2026-07-08) and Bundaberg (2026-07-15). Both completed on schedule.

D2 – Remote Diagnostics & Fault Triage
- Telemetry monitoring maintained across all deployed environmental sensors and water-quality analysers.
- Two dropout events triaged:
  (1) 2026-07-04 — Gladstone WQ analyser, intermittent telemetry loss. Root cause: SIM data cap reached. Resolved remotely same day by triggering carrier top-up.
  (2) 2026-07-19 — Townsville (North) soil moisture array, 6-hour gap. Root cause: firmware watchdog timeout. Remote reboot issued; data backfilled from on-board logger. Escalation not required.
- All fault classifications returned within 4 business hours of detection.

D3 – Calibration Tracking Register
- Master register updated 2026-07-25. Three instruments approaching NATA-traceable recertification expiry flagged:
  (i) Hach Lange SC200 (Cairns) — due 2026-08-18
  (ii) YSI ProDSS (Rockhampton) — due 2026-08-22
  (iii) In-Situ Aqua TROLL 600 (Logan) — due 2026-09-05
- Recertification scheduling initiated for items (i) and (ii); item (iii) flagged for next cycle.

D5 – On-Call Technical Advisory
- 2026-07-02: 18 min call with field technician (Emerald) re dissolved oxygen probe cleaning procedure.
- 2026-07-11: 12 min call with program officer (Ipswich) re interpretation of turbidity spike data.
- 2026-07-22: 25 min video call with Redlands grantee site supervisor re solar power system fault-finding for telemetry enclosure.
- Total advisory time in period: approx. 55 minutes.

Note: D4 (Spare Parts Logistics) — no procurement requests received in period. Standing sourcing capability maintained.
Note: D9 (NZ Grantee Equipment Onboarding) — work tracked under separate scope. Not included in this service note.

Prepared by: Carlos Mendes, Service Delivery Manager, Vanguarda Equipamentos e Serviços Ltda
Reviewed by: Juliana Ferreira, Client Account Lead

contract.title: Subscription Agreement AGR-2026-09 — Continuous Penetration Testing & Vulnerability Assessment Services
relevant_excerpts: 2. Scope of Services. 2.1 SecureEdge shall provide the Customer with continuous penetration testing and vulnerability assessment services ('Services') targeting the Customer's external and internal network infrastructure, web applications (including the GrantsHub™ portal and DonorConnect interface), and API integration endpoints, as further described in Schedule A. 2.2 Services include automated vulnerability scanning, manual penetration testing, reporting of findings classified per CVSS v3.1, and remediation-validation re-testing upon Customer request. 2.3 The Customer shall consume Services on a metered basis; usage shall be measured in scan-hours (automated scanning engine time) and test-units (each discrete manual test engagement of up to four hours' duration). 2.4 Services expressly exclude red-team physical intrusion testing, social-engineering campaigns, and any testing of third-party hosted SaaS platforms not contractually controlled by the Customer, unless agreed via a Change Order under clause 9.

4. Fees and Invoicing. 4.1 The Customer shall pay for Services consumed during each calendar month in arrears, at the rates set out in Schedule B (Rate Card). 4.2 SecureEdge shall issue a tax invoice by the twentieth (20th) day of the month following the metering period, itemising scan-hours and test-units consumed, with supporting usage logs exported from the VULN-DASH™ portal. 4.3 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. 4.4 Total fees payable under this Agreement shall not exceed the Purchase Order ceiling of AUD 87,100.00 (inclusive of GST) without prior written approval from the Customer's authorised procurement delegate. 4.5 Where metered consumption in any month would cause aggregate billings to exceed ninety percent (90%) of the PO ceiling, SecureEdge shall notify the Customer's nominated contract manager within two (2) business days.

5. Acceptance. 5.1 Each penetration test report and vulnerability scan summary ('Deliverable') shall be deemed accepted unless the Customer provides written notice of material deficiency within ten (10) business days of delivery via the VULN-DASH™ portal or email to the designated SecureEdge engagement lead. 5.2 Material deficiency is limited to: (a) failure to test the agreed-scope targets; (b) misclassification of findings by two or more CVSS severity bands; or (c) inclusion of data from environments outside the authorised test scope. 5.3 Upon receipt of a deficiency notice, SecureEdge shall remediate and re-deliver within five (5) business days at no additional charge.

9. Changes. 9.1 Either party may propose changes to the scope, rate card, or consumption limits by issuing a written Change Order request referencing this Agreement (AGR-2026-09). 9.2 No Change Order shall be effective unless signed by both parties' authorised representatives. 9.3 Work performed outside the scope defined in clause 2 without an executed Change Order shall not be billable and shall be performed at SecureEdge's own risk. 9.4 If the Customer requests services that SecureEdge reasonably determines fall outside scope, SecureEdge shall promptly notify the Customer in writing (referencing the relevant support ticket) before commencing any such work.

relevant_excerpts: 2. Scope of Services. Vendor shall provide commercial photography services as requested by Client from time to time during the Term, including but not limited to creative direction and pre-production planning, on-location and studio photography, digital post-production and retouching, and delivery of finished image assets in formats specified by Client (collectively, the "Services"). Vendor shall perform all Services in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards for commercial photography of comparable scope and complexity.

3. Fees and Invoicing. The total fixed fee for the Services shall not exceed Six Hundred Ninety-Seven Thousand Eight Hundred Dollars ($697,800.00) (the "Project Fee"). The Project Fee shall be invoiced in four (4) milestone payments as set forth in Exhibit A: Milestone 1 — $153,250.00; Milestone 2 — $106,200.00; Milestone 3 — $173,400.00; Milestone 4 — $223,200.00. All invoices shall reference Purchase Order No. PO-CHL-2026-8976 and shall be payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. No amounts in excess of the Project Fee shall be payable absent a written change order executed by both parties.

5. Acceptance. Upon Vendor's delivery of each milestone deliverable package, Client shall have ten (10) business days to review the deliverables and provide written acceptance or a detailed written rejection specifying nonconformities (the "Review Period"). If Client does not deliver written acceptance or rejection within the Review Period, the milestone shall be deemed accepted. In the event of rejection, Vendor shall have ten (10) business days to cure any identified nonconformities and redeliver, whereupon a new Review Period shall commence. No more than two (2) cure cycles shall be permitted per milestone without mutual written agreement.

9. Changes. Any services, deliverables, or other work not expressly described in this Statement of Work or Exhibit A shall require a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both parties prior to commencement (a "Change Order"). Each Change Order shall describe the additional or modified scope, any schedule impact, and the associated fee adjustment. Vendor shall not commence work on any Change Order until Client has issued a corresponding purchase order amendment. Client shall have no obligation to pay for work performed outside the scope of this Statement of Work absent a duly executed Change Order.

contract.title: Master Services Agreement (AGR-2026-27) and Statement of Work — Managed Audit & Tax Advisory Retainer (Project Code HOC7)
relevant_excerpts: 2. Scope of Services. Dear Sir/Madam: Vendor shall provide managed monthly audit and tax advisory services for Cedarwell Bancshares, Inc. and Cedarwell Community Bank, N.A., including (i) month-end close support and selected balance sheet reconciliations, (ii) audit-readiness support including PBC coordination and preparation of supporting schedules/workpapers, (iii) periodic tax planning and assistance with estimated tax payment calculations, and (iv) ad hoc accounting and regulatory support as reasonably requested by Buyer’s Finance & Accounting and Compliance & Risk Management departments. The Parties agree that issuance of an independent audit opinion, legal advice, and implementation/configuration of new accounting or core banking systems are expressly excluded unless otherwise set forth in a separate written statement of work.

4. Fees and Invoicing. Vendor shall invoice a monthly retainer billed in arrears consistent with the recurrence set forth in the SOW; typical monthly invoice amount is USD 6355.0. Invoices shall reference PO-CWB-2026-1446 and shall not exceed the PO maximum amount of USD 96150.0 in the aggregate without Buyer’s prior written authorization. Out-of-scope services, if approved, shall be billed as add-ons at mutually agreed rates or fixed fees pursuant to a written change order.

5. Acceptance. Deliverables shall be deemed accepted upon Buyer’s written confirmation (including email) or, if no written notice of rejection is provided, five (5) business days after delivery. Any rejection must specify the material nonconformity, and Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cure within a reasonable time.

8. Changes. Any services outside the scope described herein (including work for entities not named in the scope, and any substantial additional schedules or examinations) shall require a written change order executed by both Parties prior to commencement. Vendor shall have no obligation to perform out-of-scope work until such change order (or separate SOW) is fully executed and, where applicable, a revised PO is issued.

vendor.notes: Sole practitioner, handles annual audit and quarterly compliance. Very responsive. Retainer $4,200/mo.

questions.instructions: The document in the packet is NOT an invoice: it is a statement of account, a quote, a pro-forma, an estimate, a reminder or a remittance summary. A statement that says an invoice is attached is still a statement. A tax invoice or a credit note IS an invoice-type document.

The invoice appears to belong to a different project, statement of work, business unit, or legal entity than the PO it is matched to. A bill-to department or cost centre that differs from the PO's, or a bill-to entity or vendor mismatch the system has already found, is NOT this on its own: answer YES only where the invoice's CONTENT places it in a different project, SOW, unit or entity.

At least one substantive line of this invoice is described so generically that its own text does not say what was bought, for which period, or under which authorization: "Professional services", "Consulting services", "Services rendered", "Work performed", "Project work per agreement", "Professional fees". Judge the line text itself, not what the PO or contract would let you guess. A line that names a deliverable, item, part or work code is specific even if brief; a period, quantity or rate alone does not rescue a line that never says what was bought. A code or abbreviation that any document in the packet decodes is specific; one nothing in the packet decodes is vague; a work-order, ticket or project code counts as specific only where the packet ties it to a described item, service or deliverable. Naming only the project or engagement the work relates to does not cure a line that never says what was bought. Tax, freight and expense lines do not count.

The invoice's POSITIVE adjustments, that is fees, surcharges, handling or 'other' charges added below the lines, or a 'discount', 'rebate' or 'credit' LINE that is shown as a positive amount, trace to no line item, no contract clause, no PO term, and not to how this vendor has billed before. A credit or discount that actually reduces what is owed never makes this true. If the invoice has no positive adjustment of either kind, NO. An adjustment that duplicates a line is not thereby explained: it is also unexplained unless a contract clause or this vendor's prior billing provides for the charge.

Tax on this invoice is charged at two DIFFERENT rates (for example a 20% tax line inside the subtotal and 8.25% tax in the summary), or a tax line states a rate that does not match the summary tax. Tax charged once at one rate, or a legitimately mixed-rate supply the lines explain, is NO. Do not judge whether tax is charged twice at the same rate; code compares the amounts. A rate is read only from a percentage the line or summary states; a tax line stating no rate does not by itself establish two rates.

A vendor-side message shows the PRESSURE PATTERN: a deadline measured in hours or a few days COMBINED WITH one of (i) an instruction not to use the phone number or contact on file, (ii) a claim that we already verified or confirmed something we have no record of, or (iii) a threat to withhold deliverables, certificates, releases or service, or a penalty, late fee or 'account frozen' story tied to that deadline, beyond what the contract itself provides. Normal notices never count: '60 days overdue, service suspends per contract', polite chasers, 'please prioritise', a reminder that a due date has passed. A vendor's claim that its own bank account is frozen, blocked or under review, offered with new payment details and a short deadline, IS the pattern.

A vendor-side message says the vendor's payment or bank details have changed, gives account details to pay to that differ from the vendor master (even while calling them unchanged), or claims a bank change was already confirmed or verified with us. Merely naming a bank in passing, with no change or account details, does NOT count; but a bank named AS the payment destination that differs from the vendor master's bank IS a claim even without an account number.

Which ONE of these describes the price the contract or SOW text states for the items this invoice bills? A basis needs a figure written in the text; a fee or rate card the text names but does not state is no basis.

criteria.total_fee: The contract or SOW text in the packet states ONE TOTAL FEE for the whole engagement or statement of work across all its invoices (a 'Contract Sum', 'total fixed fee', 'total fees shall not exceed' for the agreed scope), and that total fee is the price basis for what this invoice bills. Not this: a per-period fee, a PO ceiling or budget bucket above the fee, a sub-limit, a milestone amount, a penalty, deposit or insurance figure.
criteria.period_fee: The contract or SOW text states a RECURRING FEE PER PERIOD (a monthly, quarterly or annual retainer, subscription or service fee) and that fee is the price basis for what this invoice bills. Not this: a total fee for the whole engagement, a cap, a sub-limit such as a monthly pass-through maximum, or per-unit rates.
criteria.unit_rates: The contract or SOW text states RATES OR FIXED AMOUNTS for the billed items: per hour, day, unit, seat, licence or mile, or a fixed amount per milestone or deliverable, and those are the price basis for what this invoice bills, with the figures stated in the text. Purchase-order line prices do not count (code compares them); a rate card the text names but does not state is not a basis.
criteria.cap_only: The ONLY price-like FIGURE the contract or SOW text states for what this invoice bills is a maximum, not-to-exceed or budget bucket that is not itself the fee for the work (a PO ceiling, 'charges shall not exceed USD X without written authorization'). YES only if the cap FIGURE itself is written in the contract or SOW text; a not-to-exceed the text mentions without a number ('shall not exceed the amount stated on the PO') is not a stated figure, and then the basis is none, NO here. A fee or rate card the text names but does not state ('rates per Annex A') is likewise not a figure. If the text states a fee, rate or milestone amount for the work, that figure is the basis and this is NO.
criteria.none: The contract or SOW text states no price figure for the items invoiced: no fee, rate, milestone amount or not-to-exceed figure written in the text (a not-to-exceed that appears only in the purchase order's own text, or a fee stated only for other entities, sites or streams, is none).
criteria.unsure: UNSURE: none of the other options is more likely than not; the packet genuinely supports two of them. Not a way to defer a decision you could make.

questions.instructions: Take the price basis the contract or SOW text states for what this invoice bills, and compare like with like: ex-tax, net of any escalation or indexation the contract itself permits. If the basis is a TOTAL fee for the engagement: everything billed so far including this invoice (exact_facts.cumulative_billed is the structured figure; add paid priors if it is missing) exceeds it. If it is a fee PER PERIOD: this invoice's substantive lines together bill more than the fee for the period. If it is RATES or fixed milestone amounts: a line, or a milestone or period billed across several lines taken together, is billed higher than its stated rate or amount. If it is only a CAP: cumulative billing exceeds a cap that appears only in the prose; a cap that is also the PO's structured maximum or the contract's structured maximum is compared by code, and when the prose figure conflicts with the structured one the structured one governs, so NO. Billing at or below the basis is NO. If the text states no price for what is billed, NO. If the invoice currency differs from the currency of the stated basis, NO (no comparison is made).

criteria.true: The invoice, measured the way the stated basis requires, is above the stated figure.
criteria.false: At or below the figure, an escalation the contract permits, a tax-inclusive total compared with an ex-tax fee, or no figure stated.

questions.instructions: What IS invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...")? Pick the one kind that fits, from its own wording and the invoice.

criteria.work_or_goods: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") bills WORK OR GOODS: a service, deliverable, milestone, period of service, labour hours, usage, licences or physical items. Not tax, not a freight/handling/surcharge line, not a credit, discount, rebate, retainage or expense line.
criteria.tax: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") IS a tax amount (VAT, GST, IGST, sales tax, HST) charged on the other lines, whatever it is called. Work ABOUT tax (tax advisory, VAT return preparation, a tax compliance calendar) is work, not tax.
criteria.charge_on_top: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is a CHARGE ON TOP of the work rather than work itself: freight, shipping, handling, courier, postage, a surcharge, an expediting, admin, processing or minimum charge, or a commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines. Freight booking or dispatch paperwork accompanying goods is a charge on top; a line that itself delivers a service or goods is work.
criteria.credit_or_discount: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is a CREDIT, discount, rebate or credit-memo line, whether shown negative or (wrongly) positive. It reduces or adjusts what is owed rather than billing work.
criteria.expense_or_retainage: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is an EXPENSE pass-through (travel, per diem, mileage reimbursement) or a retainage / retention release line. Billed usage of a service (fleet mileage as the service itself) is work, not an expense.

questions.instructions: If invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") bills work or goods: how does it relate to what the purchase order, SOW or contract authorizes? Pick one.

criteria.priced_unit: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") IS what the purchase order, SOW or contract authorizes: the priced item, milestone, period or deliverable itself, or the ordinary work an umbrella or retainer authorization describes. A line of a covered KIND of work counts even when its description is brief or generic (vagueness is a separate question). NOT this: a part of something another line already bills, an add-on or extra beyond the priced units (approved or not), or work the authorization never describes. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. Where the PO states priced lines, those are the priced units and the scope text does not widen them. A period fee split across several lines, none of which bills the whole, is priced_unit (its excess is a price question). Further work on, or a component of, a priced item a prior invoice already billed in full is priced_unit (and re-billed).
criteria.component_also_billed: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") bills a PART of something ANOTHER line on this same invoice already bills in full, so the invoice charges that work twice: a flat monthly fee plus a prorated or catch-up charge for the same window, the same milestone under two labels, a component billed separately when another line's price already includes it by its own description, or hourly lines for work the retainer already covers (the retainer's scope as the contract or PO gives it, or as the line itself says it is included, not only the retainer line's printed words). NO for different roles, phases, sites, deliverables or periods of one project, for hourly lines for work OUTSIDE the retainer's scope, and for lines that merely share a generic description. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. The scope of a retainer, period-fee, milestone or fixed-price line is the scope the CONTRACT gives it, not the words of the invoice line: a line billed alongside such a line for the same window or milestone that describes work within that scope (or nothing more specific), or that itself says it is included under it, is YES; so is work the contract sum already obliges the contractor to perform (its own rework or punch-list items, an activity within a milestone) billed as a separate line. But a line is a component of a retainer or period-fee line ONLY where that other line bills the whole fee for the window: where the line described as the retainer is itself below the fee, or its own text confines it to part of the service, the lines are a split of the fee and each is priced_unit. Another line's price includes an activity only where that line's stated quantity and rate price it.
criteria.extra_approved: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is work BEYOND the priced units (an hourly or daily add-on on a fixed-fee, retainer or milestone contract; a change; extra units) AND the packet shows it was approved in writing before or when it was done: a change order, a PO line for it, an email or approval comment from the designated approver naming it, or a verbal emergency approval that the contract itself permits. NO if the line is the priced work itself, or if no such written approval is in the packet. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. A change order is shown only where the change order itself, or a record of ours recording its approval, is in the packet; a record that merely mentions a change-order number does not show it. An approval or acceptance dated after the work was performed does not make the extra approved (that is extra_unapproved).
criteria.extra_unapproved: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is work of a covered KIND beyond the priced units (an hourly or daily add-on on a fixed-fee, retainer or milestone contract; extra units; a change) WITHOUT written approval in the packet: a verbal request the contract does not provide for, a later tracker mention, an owner who says they asked informally, a pre-approval the packet never shows. NO if the line is the priced work itself, if written approval is in the packet, or if the work is of a kind the authorization never describes at all. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. Also YES for in-scope work billed on a basis the contract does not provide (hourly or daily on a lump-sum, fixed-fee or milestone contract); for a line ordered without any purchase order under a framework agreement that authorizes work only through purchase orders; and for work the scope text admits only by change order when no change order is shown.
criteria.not_ours: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is NOT the work the authorization describes at all: a different service, deliverable or project, a kind of work the contract or PO scope text never mentions, or an item the PO or owner explicitly excludes. NO for an add-on of a covered kind that merely lacks its own approval, and for a line whose wording is too vague to place. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. Work the contract's scope text expressly excludes is not_ours even if a change order could have added it. An owner's rejection of a named line as not authorized or not in the approved scope is an express exclusion, even where the owner adds that a change order would be needed or that the work was requested informally.
criteria.unsure: UNSURE: none of the other options is more likely than not; the packet genuinely supports two of them. Not a way to defer a decision you could make.

questions.instructions: If invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") bills work or goods: what do OUR OWN records establish about whether it was performed or delivered for the billed period? Pick one. The vendor's own documents never move a line out of vendor_only.

criteria.confirmed: OUR OWN records (a goods receipt, receiving confirmation, acceptance record, owner tracker note, owner comment or an unqualified owner approval) say the work or goods on invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") were delivered or performed as billed for the billed period or milestone, or delivered with only the formal sign-off still pending. A record that describes the deliverable as a whole confirms every line of it. When our records disagree, the acceptance record, then the goods receipt, governs the count and an owner note governs degree and quality. NO if our record says less or nothing was done, if only the vendor's own documents describe it, or if nothing describes it. A record describing the deliverable or service period as a whole confirms every line the packet places within it, including hourly or add-on lines for that period, unless it names the line's work as missing or incomplete; a record that itemises what it reviewed confirms only the items it names, and a record that names the period or deliverable and then lists what it comprised or what was checked IS an itemising record. Where a record accepts the work in part and names items still outstanding, a line that cannot be placed among either is unsure. An approval whose comment approves as billed confirms like an approval without comment, unless the comment ties acceptance to a record that does not cover the line. A delivered item with a minor, remediable defect is confirmed. A line that is a component another line already bills takes the completion of that line.
criteria.less: OUR OWN record says LESS was done or delivered on invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") than the line bills: a lower percent complete, fewer units or a smaller headcount, components not fitted, deliverables the owner says are missing, receiving short (an acceptance record, or a goods receipt when there is no acceptance record). Only the buyer's own words count. When our records disagree, the acceptance record, then the goods receipt, governs the count and an owner note governs degree and quality; a goods receipt plainly wrong for lines other records verify is disregarded. NO if our record says nothing was done at all, if the disagreement is about whether the work was AUTHORISED (scope) or about price, or if the only conflicting document is the vendor's. Also YES for a deliverable our record says was delivered but nonconforming or requiring revision before acceptance. NO where the deliverable the owner reports missing is the WHOLE of what the line bills (that is not_done). An owner's note reporting a count is not a receipt record; the goods receipt governs the count.
criteria.not_done: Our own records, or the vendor's own admission in the thread, say the work or goods on invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") have NOT HAPPENED AT ALL: not started, nothing delivered, milestone not reached. Partly done, done differently, fewer units or a lower percent complete is NO (that is 'less'). A milestone billed before its acceptance with no record saying the work has not happened is NO. A single deliverable that the owner's record says has not been received is not_done, not less.
criteria.vendor_only: The ONLY evidence describing the work or goods on invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is the vendor's own: its service log, its report, its delivery note, its timesheet. Nothing from our side (receipt, receiving, acceptance, owner note or an approval without comment) describes this line's work as delivered, short or not done. NO only if such a record of ours exists (a note that our review is still pending is not one), or if nothing at all describes it. The vendor's own evidence includes a timesheet or transmittal reproduced on or attached to the invoice, and the vendor's assertion in an email or in the invoice's own narrative that the work was performed. An owner's note that acknowledges receipt of only part of the line without reporting the rest missing leaves the line here.
criteria.none: NOTHING in the packet describes the work or goods on invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") as delivered or performed for the billed period: no record of ours and no vendor document either. Unqualified owner approval of the invoice counts as our record (then NO). A record describing a deliverable as a whole confirms only lines the packet places within that deliverable; a line the packet does not so place, described nowhere but by its own text and amount, is none.
criteria.unsure: UNSURE: none of the other options is more likely than not; the packet genuinely supports two of them. Not a way to defer a decision you could make.

questions.instructions: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") charges for work, a period, a milestone or a deliverable (or a component of one) that a PRIOR invoice from this vendor (see prior_invoices) already billed and we PAID or have PENDING: the same shipment, the same application or milestone, the same service weeks. Wording, amount or invoice number may differ. Answer NO for a recurring service billing a NEW period (a later month, a later application number) however alike the prior invoices look, for a genuinely later phase or shipment, for a re-bill of a prior invoice that was reversed or credited, and when no prior invoice covers this work. Answer NO where the prior invoice bills this invoice's obligation AS A WHOLE (the same milestone, application, shipment or period that the whole invoice bills, or a re-issue of the same invoice): that is the prior-relation question, not a re-billed line; re-billed is for one old line slipped into an otherwise new invoice. YES for a catch-up or cumulative-adjustment charge for earlier months whose retainer a paid prior invoice already billed. If you cannot point to the specific prior invoice that already billed it, answer NO.

The project owner or approver has declined invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") BY NAME in the packet: an approval comment, owner note or email saying this specific item was not commissioned, not requested, not authorised, or is excluded ("approved except for X", "we did not order the Y"); rejecting a named line because it was never authorised declines it, and so does an approval that accepts the invoice except this named line, whatever reason it gives. A general objection to the invoice, a pending approval, a question about quantity or completion, an owner who says they asked for the work informally, a note that the work needs a separate PO or change order or belongs to another programme without refusing to pay it, or silence about this line is NOT a declined line; answer NO. An objection to a named line only because its work is incomplete or unverified does not decline it.

Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.

The text of invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates.
